title: Digital public infrastructure is becoming a gendered access system whose value depends on inclusive design, safeguards, and measurable use
source_unit: UN Women, Co-Develop, and Centre for Digital Public Infrastructure, Making digital public infrastructure work for women and girls: Exemplar stories
geography: Global gender-inclusive digital-public-infrastructure examples across financial inclusion, essential services, digital identity, payments, and data exchange

observations.period: 2026; digital public infrastructure and gender equality

denominator.unit: UN Women global publication and exemplar-case framework

dpi_infrastructure_role.value: digital public infrastructure is increasingly used to enable financial inclusion and access to essential services

gender_gap.value: efforts to use DPI to advance gender equality remain at an early stage

capability_condition.value: DPI can deliver society-wide capabilities only when it responds to the needs and constraints of women and girls

system_components.value: digital identity, payments, and data exchange are treated as core components of gender-inclusive DPI

observations.method: UN Women, Co-Develop, and CDPI synthesis of exemplar stories and the DPI Safeguards Framework, connecting digital systems with gender equality and service access.
observations.uncertainty: The publication is a case-study and policy framework, not a global adoption census, representative user survey, or causal estimate of DPI effects on women and girls.
observations.subgroup: Women and girls, people seeking public services, users of digital identity and payments, governments, regulators, donors, technology providers, and civil-society advocates.
observations.counterinterpretation: DPI can reduce access friction and expand capability, but digital channels can also create exclusion, surveillance, safety, or dependency risks when alternatives and safeguards are weak.

observations.period: 2026; life-course access to digital public infrastructure

life_course.value: gender-inclusive DPI should recognize women’s experiences across the life cycle, from birth registration through support in older years

access_pathways.value: identity, payments, and data exchange can connect people to finance, public services, and rights across different life stages

design_requirement.value: women’s needs and experiences should shape design, development, deployment, reflection, and review

agency_endpoint.value: the intended endpoint is not connection alone but safer, more equitable access to capabilities, resources, and services

observations.method: Life-course policy framing supported by exemplar stories and the DPI Safeguards Framework.
observations.uncertainty: Life-course coverage does not show that one digital architecture meets all needs; age, disability, income, language, geography, documentation, household power, and offline alternatives remain relevant.
observations.subgroup: Girls and women at different life stages, older women, people without documentation or stable connectivity, caregivers, and users of identity, payment, and service systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: A life-course lens can improve continuity while still requiring human assistance, non-digital routes, privacy protections, and local institutional capacity.

observations.period: 2026; safeguards, participation, and gendered system risk

safeguard_route.value: gender-inclusive DPI is presented as requiring safeguards that account for women’s experiences and unequal risks

co_design.value: women and girls should participate in designing and building systems from the start

measurement.value: gender-disaggregated data on awareness, access, use, and impacts are recommended

risk_boundary.value: system availability is not equivalent to safe, meaningful, or equitable use

observations.method: Policy and safeguard synthesis across exemplar digital-public-infrastructure initiatives, with attention to design, implementation, use, and review.
observations.uncertainty: The publication identifies safeguard requirements and case examples but does not quantify prevalence of harms or establish comparative effects across systems.
observations.subgroup: Women and girls with different access, safety, documentation, literacy, disability, income, and connectivity conditions; system designers and public authorities.
observations.counterinterpretation: Disaggregated measurement can expose unequal use and improve design, but measurement alone does not create remedy, representation, or institutional accountability.

observations.period: 2026; recommended public and private implementation routes

denominator.unit: UN Women gender-inclusive DPI recommendation set

investment.value: invest at scale in gender-inclusive DPI to address challenges faced by women and girls

co_creation.value: design and build DPI with and by women and girls, including their perspectives across the full system cycle

data_feedback.value: collect gender-disaggregated evidence on awareness, access, use, and impacts to guide review and correction

actor_set.value: governments, regulators, donors, technology providers, and civil society all have roles in making DPI safer and more equitable

observations.method: Synthesis of exemplar cases and recommendations for public, private, donor, regulatory, and civil-society actors.
observations.uncertainty: The recommendations are not a delivery evaluation or funding audit; implementation depends on procurement, governance, interoperability, privacy, local capacity, and political accountability.
observations.subgroup: Women and girls, public-service users, digital-system operators, regulators, donors, technology firms, and civil-society organizations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Scaling can widen reach but also scale exclusion or harm; phased deployment, meaningful co-design, safeguards, and correction routes remain necessary.

related_sources.claim: UN Women publication catalogue entry and related 2026 gender-technology resources.
Related UN Women publication on gendered access to assistive technology.

boundary: This record adds a gendered digital-public-infrastructure route across identity, payments, data exchange, financial inclusion, essential services, life-course access, safeguards, co-design, and accountability. It uses an exemplar-story and policy framework publication, not a global adoption census, raw user-level data, representative gender-attitudes survey, causal impact evaluation, or proof that DPI delivers equitable outcomes without offline alternatives and remedy.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UN Women publication page reviewed for the DPI role, early-stage gender-equality gap, life-course framing, system components, safeguards, co-design, disaggregated measurement, and three recommendations.
